title: Collision Exclusion for Original OTR Masks
summary: Trivial collisions are known for special defining polynomials, but a general formal argument excluding collisions among the original OTR masks remains unavailable.

formal_statement.body: For the original OTR mask polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$, develop a general formal collision-exclusion argument parameterized by $n\in\mathbb{N}$, a primitive polynomial $P$ defining $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ such that $X$ generates $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}^{*}$, and an integer $t$ with $2<t\le 2^{n/2}$. The argument should prove that no masks indexed by $i,j\in[2,t]$ collide. No general formal argument establishing this exclusion is currently available.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of the original OTR authenticated-encryption mask polynomials over binary finite fields.
assumptions: The defining polynomial P is primitive, and X generates the multiplicative group of F₂ⁿ.
parameters: n ∈ ℕ: the extension degree defining the field F₂ⁿ
P: the polynomial defining the chosen representation of F₂ⁿ
t: an integer setting the upper mask-index limit, with 2 < t ≤ 2^(n/2)
i and j: mask indices drawn from [2, t]
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop a general formal argument proving that no original OTR masks indexed by i and j in [2, t] collide under these conditions.

citations.label: Trick or Tweak: On the (In)security of OTR's Tweaks

progress.summary: The source identifies the absence of a general formal collision-exclusion argument and reports trivial collisions for special defining polynomials, particularly trinomials and pentanomials. The general exclusion task remains open.
citation_labels: Raphael Bost et al., Trick or Tweak: On the (In)security of OTR's Tweaks
